issues.description: No documentation of capture group syntax and usage in replacements
issues.should_add: Comprehensive capture group documentation: numbered groups ($0, $1, $2, etc.), named groups ($name), and brace syntax (${1}, ${name})
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add detailed section on capture groups:
- $0 represents the entire match
- $1, $2, etc. for numbered capture groups (based on opening parenthesis position)
- $name for named capture groups
- ${1}, ${name} brace syntax to disambiguate from following text
- $$ to write a literal $
- Examples: 'rg '(\w+) (\w+)' -r '$2 $1'' to swap words, 'rg '(?P<year>\d{4})' -r 'Year: ${year}'' for named groups
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/defs.rs:5999-6021 (capture group documentation in flag help), crates/matcher/src/interpolate.rs:3-56 (interpolation implementation)

issues.description: No documentation of the specific syntax rules for capture group references
issues.should_add: Detailed syntax rules: valid characters in names ([_0-9A-Za-z]), how names are parsed, brace requirement for special cases
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section explaining:
- Capture group names consist of letters, numbers, and underscores only ([_0-9A-Za-z])
- Longest matching name is used (e.g., $1a matches name '1a', not group 1 followed by 'a')
- Use braces ${1}a to separate group reference from following text
- Invalid group references are replaced with empty string
- Show examples of edge cases: $1a (name), ${1}a (group 1 + 'a'), $foo (named group)

issues.description: No documentation of shell quoting requirements when using replacements
issues.should_add: Shell quoting best practices to avoid variable expansion
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add important note about shell quoting:
- Use single quotes in Bash/zsh to prevent shell variable expansion
- Wrong: rg '(\w+)' -r "$1" (shell expands $1)
- Correct: rg '(\w+)' -r '$1' (ripgrep processes $1)
- Explain that without proper quoting, $1 gets replaced by shell variable (likely empty)
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/defs.rs:6017-6019 (shell quoting warning in help text)

issues.description: No explanation of how replacements affect output and interaction with other flags
issues.should_add: Documentation of replacement behavior and interaction with other output flags
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section explaining:
- Replacements are output-only (files are never modified)
- By default, replaces each match, not entire line (to replace entire line, match entire line)
- Works with --only-matching flag
- Show example: 'rg '(\w+)@(\w+\.com)' -o -r '$1 at $2' to extract and format email parts
- Clarify that replacement text appears in output instead of original match

issues.description: No working examples demonstrating replacement functionality
issues.should_add: Multiple practical examples showing common replacement patterns and use cases
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add examples section with:
1. Simple literal replacement: 'rg foo -r bar'
2. Swapping words: 'rg '(\w+) (\w+)' -r '$2 $1''
3. Named groups: 'rg '(?P<name>\w+)' -r 'Hello, ${name}!''
4. Extracting parts: 'rg '(\d{3})-(\d{3})-(\d{4})' -r 'Area code: $1' -o'
5. Escaping dollar sign: 'rg price -r '$$5.00''
6. Using with context lines: 'rg pattern -r replacement -C2'
7. Multiple matches per line replacement

issues.description: No examples or explanation specific to named capture groups in regex patterns
issues.should_add: Detailed explanation and examples of using named capture groups with replacements
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add section on named capture groups:
- Regex syntax: (?P<name>pattern) for Rust regex, (?<name>pattern) for PCRE2
- Using in replacement: $name or ${name}
- Benefits: self-documenting patterns, more maintainable
- Example: 'rg '(?P<protocol>https?)://(?P<domain>[^/]+)' -r '$protocol at $domain''
- Show comparison with numbered groups for same pattern
